results.claim: Exact stationary rarity. For 0<p<1, put α=1-p. If π is the stationary law, then the complete-state probability is Π_{n,p}:=π([n])=∏_{r=1}^n [rα^r/(n-(n-r)α^r)]. Equivalently, R_{n,p}:=Π_{n,p}^{-1}=∏_{r=1}^n [1+(n/r)(α^{-r}-1)].
results.proof_sketch: The finite chain is irreducible, so its unique stationary law is permutation invariant. For a fixed r-set A let M_r=Pr_π(A⊆S), with M_0=1. Conditional on the new draw, A is present immediately before losses either when the draw is outside A and A was already present, or when the draw is i∈A and A\{i} was present. All r members must then survive. Thus M_r=α^r[(1-r/n)M_r+(r/n)M_{r-1}], giving M_r/M_{r-1}=rα^r/[n-(n-r)α^r]. Multiplication yields M_n=π([n]). Taking reciprocals factorwise gives [n-(n-r)α^r]/(rα^r)=1+(n/r)(α^{-r}-1).

results.claim: Finite-n hitting-time sandwich. Let H_n=∑_{j=1}^n 1/j and A_{n,p}:=(R_{n,p}-1)/(1-α^n). Then for every n and 0<p<1, A_{n,p}≤E[T_{n,p}]≤H_n A_{n,p}.
results.proof_sketch:
Let h_k be the mean time to hit n from size k and e_k=h_k-h_{k+1}. Upward skip-freeness and the strong Markov property identify e_k with the mean passage time k→k+1. Couple chains from nested sets of sizes k and k+1 using the same draw and survival bits; nesting and a size gap at most one persist. When the upper chain first reaches k+2, the lower has already reached k+1, so e_k≤e_{k+1}.

Put u_k=(n-k)α^{k+1}/n and F_k(r)=Pr_k(K_1≤r). First-step analysis gives u_ke_k=1+Σ_{r<k}e_rF_k(r). The same nested coupling implies Σ_{r=j}^{k-1}F_k(r)≥Σ_{r=j}^{k-2}F_{k-1}(r). Writing each increasing e_r in terms of its nonnegative increments is Abel summation, and shows that the recurrence numerator is nondecreasing. Hence (n-k)e_k=nα^{-(k+1)}[1+Σ_{r<k}e_rF_k(r)] is nondecreasing. Therefore h_0=Σe_k≤e_{n-1}H_n.

Kac's return identity at n, where K_1∼Bin(n,α), gives R=1+Σ_{k<n}Pr_n(K_1=k)h_k. Thus A is a convex combination of h_0,…,h_{n-1}. Since h_{n-1}=e_{n-1}≤A≤h_0, the sandwich follows.

results.claim: Asymptotic closure throughout the non-classical range. For every fixed η>0, uniformly over η(log n)/n²≤p_n<1, E[T_{n,p_n}]=(1+o(1))A_{n,p_n}=(1+o(1))(R_{n,p_n}-1)/(1-(1-p_n)^n).
results.proof_sketch:
The passage recurrence and the event that an already-held coupon is drawn and at least one held coupon is lost give e_k/e_{k-1}≥F_k(k-1)/u_k≥k(1-α^k)/[(n-k)α^{k+1}]. Let m=⌊n/2⌋ and β=m(1-α^m). Uniformly in the stated range, β≥c_η log n: if mp≤1, then 1-α^m≥1-e^{-mp}≥mp/2, while if mp>1 it is at least 1-e^{-1}.

For a_j=e_{n-j}/e_{n-1} and J=⌊β/2⌋, the relevant indices satisfy n-j≥m and a_{j+1}≤(j/β)a_j. Hence Σ_{j=2}^J a_j=O(1/β) and a_J≤β^{-1}2^{-J+2}. Monotonicity of (n-k)e_k gives j a_j≤J a_J for j≥J, so the remaining tail is at most Ja_J(1+log(n/J))=o_η(1). Consequently h_0/e_{n-1}=Σ_{j=1}^n a_j=1+o_η(1), uniformly. Since e_{n-1}≤A≤h_0, squeezing proves both displayed equivalences.

results.claim: The resulting regimes differ from the product-of-marginals prediction. (i) If p=γ(log n)/n² with fixed γ>0, then E[T_{n,p}]∼n^{γ+1}/(γ log n). (ii) If (log n)/n²≪p≪1/n, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼n²p. (iii) If p=c/n with fixed c>0, then n^{-1}log E[T_{n,p}]→I(c):=∫_0^1 log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x)dx>log(1+c). (iv) If np→∞, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼(n²/2)log(1/(1-p)).
results.proof_sketch:
Write L=log R. Uniformly for p=o(1/n), α^{-r}-1=rp+O(r²p²), and expansion of the logarithm gives L=n²p+O(n³p²). At p=γ(log n)/n² this yields R∼n^γ, while 1-α^n∼γ(log n)/n; Claim 2 gives (i). In (ii), L∼n²p and |log(np)|=o(n²p), so neither the denominator nor R-1 changes the logarithmic equivalent.

For p=c/n, with ℓ_n=-log(1-c/n), nℓ_n→c. The summands are a Riemann sum for the continuous extension at zero of log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x), yielding (iii). For x>0, e^{cx}-1>cx, so the integrand exceeds log(1+c) on positive measure.

For general ℓ=-log α, exact factorization gives L=[n(n+1)/2]ℓ+nlog n-log(n!)+Σ_r log(1-(1-r/n)e^{-rℓ}). The correction has absolute value at most Σ_{r≥1}-log(1-e^{-rℓ})≤C/ℓ, while nlog n-log(n!)=O(n). If np→∞, then nℓ→∞, both errors are o(n²ℓ), and 1-α^n→1. Claim 2 then proves (iv).

final_writeup:
Let α=1-p and K_t=|S_t|. The key quantity is the exact stationary entrance rarity, rather than the product of stationary marginals proposed by the mean-field calculation.

For a fixed r-subset A, permutation invariance makes M_r=Pr_π(A⊆S) depend only on r. Conditioning on the new draw and then requiring every member of A to survive gives

M_r=α^r[(1-r/n)M_r+(r/n)M_{r-1}].

Starting from M_0=1 therefore yields

Π_{n,p}=π([n])=∏_{r=1}^n rα^r/[n-(n-r)α^r],

and

R_{n,p}=Π_{n,p}^{-1}=∏_{r=1}^n[1+(n/r)(α^{-r}-1)].

This stationary rarity must be corrected for consecutive visits to the complete state. Let h_k be the expected time to hit n from size k and e_k=h_k-h_{k+1}. Because upward jumps have size at most one, e_k is the mean passage time from k to k+1. A nested-set coupling, using common draws and common survival bits, preserves both inclusion and a size difference of at most one. It follows that e_k is nondecreasing.

A first-step calculation gives

u_ke_k=1+Σ_{r<k}e_rF_k(r),

where u_k=(n-k)α^{k+1}/n and F_k(r)=Pr_k(K_1≤r). The nested coupling also supplies the tail-CDF inequalities needed for Abel summation. Since the increments of e_r are nonnegative, the recurrence numerator is nondecreasing, and hence (n-k)e_k is nondecreasing. Consequently

h_0=Σ_{k=0}^{n-1}e_k≤H_ne_{n-1}.

Kac's return identity at n is

R_{n,p}=1+Σ_{k<n}Pr_n(K_1=k)h_k,

with K_1∼Bin(n,α). After conditioning on leaving n,

A_{n,p}:=(R_{n,p}-1)/(1-α^n)

is a convex combination of h_0,…,h_{n-1}. Thus e_{n-1}=h_{n-1}≤A_{n,p}≤h_0, proving the exact finite bound

A_{n,p}≤E[T_{n,p}]≤H_nA_{n,p}.

The factor H_n disappears uniformly in the non-classical range. The same passage recurrence gives

e_k/e_{k-1}≥k(1-α^k)/[(n-k)α^{k+1}].

With m=⌊n/2⌋ and β=m(1-α^m), the assumption p≥η(log n)/n² implies β≥c_η log n. For a_j=e_{n-j}/e_{n-1}, the last J=⌊β/2⌋ passage ratios make the earlier terms decrease geometrically; monotonicity of (n-k)e_k bounds everything before that by a vanishing harmonic tail. Explicitly,

Σ_{j=2}^J a_j=O(1/β),

and

Σ_{j≥J}a_j≤Ja_J(1+log(n/J))=o_η(1).

Therefore h_0/e_{n-1}=1+o_η(1). Squeezing A between these quantities proves

E[T_{n,p}]=(1+o(1))(R_{n,p}-1)/(1-(1-p)^n)

uniformly for every fixed η>0 and η(log n)/n²≤p<1.

Expanding this exact product resolves the source's non-classical regimes. If p=γ(log n)/n², then R∼n^γ and 1-(1-p)^n∼γ(log n)/n, so

E[T_{n,p}]∼n^{γ+1}/(γ log n).

If (log n)/n²≪p≪1/n, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼n²p. If p=c/n, then

n^{-1}log E[T_{n,p}]→∫_0^1log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x)dx,

which is strictly larger than log(1+c), the product-of-marginals rate. Finally, if np→∞,

log E[T_{n,p}]∼(n²/2)log(1/(1-p)).

Thus the preferred mean-field scale is not generally tight, but the requested lower/upper gap is fully closed by a different, exact stationary-entrance scale across every non-classical regime identified in the source.
